[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like KWEB on 2026-09-18, the median 10-session forward return was 0.68%. The distribution is wide and right-skewed, with a standard deviation of 8.19% and a worst-case outcome of -9.23%, meaning the single number to anchor on is that roughly half the time the position finished slightly positive, but the path there frequently involved drawdowns exceeding 3%.

[state]
The retrieval engine pulled these 50 analogs because KWEB's current state is defined by three distinctive features: it sits -42.74% from its 52-week high (z-score -1.899), its 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score is deeply depressed at -2.663 (z-score -1.607), and WTI crude has surged 19.24% over 20 days (z-score 1.124). These are combined with a 20-session return of -6.97% and a 20-session underperformance versus the benchmark of -7.1%. The macro backdrop shows a VIX level of 15.44, a 10y-2y Treasury slope of 0.25, and a 90-day Fed funds target change of 0.25 bp. Market sentiment registers in the Greed band with a fearGreedValue of 70. Contextual headlines framing the present include CNBC Markets reporting that "Japanese companies are retreating from China at a historic rate," and CNBC Markets noting that "Stock futures are flat as investors grapple with higher yields, await Fed minutes." Derivatives positioning data is unavailable on this card.

[history]
Over the 10-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a mean return of 1.81% and a median of 0.68%. The spread is substantial, running from a minimum of -9.23% to a maximum of 43.14%, with a skew of 2.601 driven by that single extreme upside print. The 10th percentile outcome was -5.81% and the 90th percentile was 8.66%. In 56% of the episodes the return was above zero, and in 44% it was below. The bad tail is populated by recent sessions: NKE on 2026-09-03 returned -8.41%, PDD on 2026-08-31 returned -7.05%, NKE on 2026-08-13 returned -6.77%, HD on 2026-09-03 returned -5.69%, and KWEB itself on 2026-08-31 returned -5.15%. The lone massive outlier driving the right tail is NIO on 2025-07-08, which returned 43.14%.

[tails]
A position can finish near the median and still be un-holdable along the way. The median max adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -3.3%. At the 10th percentile, the max adverse excursion reached -7.26%, and at the 25th percentile it was -5.96%. Looking at breach probabilities, 32 out of the 50 episodes saw the price breach a 5% drawdown intra-horizon. Only 2 episodes breached a 10% drawdown, and none breached 15% or 20%. On the upside, the median max favourable excursion was 4.04%, with the 75th percentile at 8.43% and the 90th percentile at 14.31%. The reward-to-risk ratio based on these excursions is 1.22.

[stress]
The baseline median for the 50 analogs is 0.68%. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario worsens the picture most severely, dropping the median to -9.75% (a delta of -10.43%), with a 10th percentile of -23.23% and a 75% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; however, central-bank backstops arrived inside that window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns, making it a sample of one regime rather than a forecast. The 2025-04 tariff shock drops the median to -3.36% (delta -4.04%) with a 65.4% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown, though policy reversals inside that window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario produces a median of -4.81% (delta -5.49%) with a 30% breach probability, but a nine-month window means the per-date cap samples it repeatedly, so it should be treated as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind yields a median of -2.77% (delta -3.45%) with a 22.2% breach probability, though the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, making H-day forward returns look benign even if the intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare gives a median of -3.08% (delta -3.76%), but it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019 that flatters late-window analogs. The 2023-03 regional bank stress actually improves the median to 4.4% (delta 3.72%), but the very short window means the analog set is dominated by a handful of sessions. Shock scenarios like vol-spike (+2 sigma VIX) produce a median of 0.67% (delta -0.01%), noting that VIX shocks mean-revert quickly so this stresses entry timing more than terminal value. Rates-up (+1.5 sigma) gives a median of -0.41% (delta -1.09%), using DGS3MO/T10Y2Y levels as proxies without accounting for name-specific duration. Liquidity
